title: VXLAN flap during tenant policy rollout - post-incident journal
content:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

On 2026-08-21 14:02 PDT a tenant-facing on-prem deployment experienced intermittent control-plane reachability and request timeouts for ~23 minutes after a targeted network policy rollout. Impact was confined to tenant A's zone-3 hosts (approx 18 nodes). Symptoms: higher p99 latency for API calls, aborted TLS handshakes to model-serving endpoints, and a spike in overlay packet drops.

Immediate customer impact: degraded inference latency and ~5% request error rate for tenant A during the incident window. No data loss observed, customer traffic resumed normal after mitigations.

DETECTION / ALERTS:
- First alert: high p99 request latency from internal synthetic probes (14:02:11).
- Second: control-plane gRPC keepalives failing to select next-hop (14:04:08).
- Network monitoring showed VXLAN encapsulation errors and rapid tunnel churn (14:05).
- PagerDuty fired for eng-private-deployments oncall; SRE responded.

TIMELINE (local times):
- 14:00 - Policy rollout started (canary batch 20% of hosts in tenant A zone-3).
- 14:02 - Synthetic latency alert.
- 14:03 - Operator noticed control-plane reconnect logs from 6 agents.
- 14:05 - netdev counters: vxlan_rx_errors and generic receive errors spike.
- 14:08 - Decision: pause rollout and rollback latest ACL change (14:09).
- 14:12 - Partial recovery observed as churn subsides.
- 14:25 - Full connectivity re-established; post-checks by SRE and SE.
- 14:45 - Incident declared mitigated; post-incident note created.

INITIAL HYPOTHESIS (what we thought during incident):
- Policy change introduced an ACL that caused previously pinned flows to rehash across tunnel endpoints, triggering large forwarding table updates on the hardware offload path. Offload path then raised encapsulation errors, dropping VXLAN inner packets and causing TLS session failures.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed):
- A combination of factors:
  1) A tenant policy rule changed L4 match (src-port rewrite for health-checks) which caused stateful hashing behavior to change;
  2) The host NIC firmware (model QX-9xx) has a known corner-case where a rapid sequence of tunnel endpoint changes causes the NIC's VXLAN offload table to overflow and print errors instead of failing gracefully;
  3) Our rollout pace (20% canary with <2m stagger) produced simultaneous rekey/flow rebalance across many hosts and pushed the NIC bug into failure mode.

EVIDENCE / LOGS (selected excerpts):
- node-az3-12 /var/log/syslog (14:05:02):
  "kernel: vxlan0: rx: vxlan_rcv_inner failed: -5 (encap table overflow)"
- control-plane-agent (14:03:45):
  "WARN grpc: keepalive timeout, reconnecting to controlplane (attempt 6)"
- sFlow summary: sudden rise in encapsulated drops between host pairs in zone-3 (14:04 - 14:07).

MITIGATION TAKEN DURING INCIDENT:
- Immediately paused the deployment (14:08).
- Rolled back the specific ACL/L4 rewrite introduced in the canary (14:09).
- Temporarily pinned VXLAN endpoints on affected hosts to avoid rehash storms (14:10) via a small host-level rule in /etc/netplan (see runbook snippet).
- Rebalanced control-plane connections by staggering reconnects (added jitter to agent restart counter) to avoid synchronized reconnections.

SHORT-TERM FIXES (done):
- Consolidated canary window to 10% with >5m stagger.
- Added a pre-rollout netdev health check that verifies vxlan_tx/rx counters are stable for 3m before proceeding.
- Notified affected customer and provided timeline and mitigation steps.

LONG-TERM ACTION ITEMS (owners + ETA):
- FW-1: Kernel/NIC firmware coordination — coordinate with infra/hardware team to test QX-9xx firmware behavior and prioritize vendor patch. Owner: Lin Zhao. ETA: 2026-09-10.
- FW-2: Rollout safety tooling — add a rollout simulator that can run policy changes against sample host snapshots to estimate flow-table churn. Owner: Miguel Santos. ETA: 2026-09-24.
- FW-3: Runbook addition — create a dedicated "VXLAN overlay offload failure" runbook entry including exact netdev checks and safe rollback playbook. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2026-08-30 (draft in review).
- Ops-1: Add alert rule: vxlan_encap_errors > 10/min AND agent_reconnects > 3 in 5m -> pager. Owner: SRE Alerts team. ETA: 2026-08-28.

RUNBOOK SNIPPETS (candidate steps for new runbook):
1) Quick triage checklist:
   - Confirm affected tenant/hosts via monitoring (tag filter tenant: A zone:3).
   - Check vxlan counters on a suspect host: sudo ethtool -S vxlan0 OR cat /sys/class/net/vxlan0/statistics/rx_errors
   - Grep kernel messages for "vxlan" or "encap" errors: sudo journalctl -k -u systemd -S '14:00:00' | grep -i vxlan
   - Verify NIC offload status: sudo ethtool -k eth0 | grep -i tx-offload

2) Safe mitigation (fast):
   - Pause rollout in the control plane console (or API): PATCH /rollouts/{id} body {"state":"paused"}
   - If symptoms persist, rollback the exact policy change (not full config) and wait 5-10 minutes for flows to re-stabilize.
   - Pin VXLAN endpoints on affected hosts (example netplan fragment):
     network:
       ethernets:
         eth0:
           dhcp4: false
           addresses: [10.0.3.12/24]
       tunnels:
         vxlan-tenantA:
           mode: vxlan
           local: 10.0.3.12
           remote: [list of static peers]  # temporary

3) Post-mitigation verification:
   - Verify rx_errors and tx_errors fall to baseline for 10m.
   - Confirm control-plane agent logs show stable gRPC connections.
   - Run synthetic probe to tenant endpoints and verify p99 latency within SLA.

COMMANDS WE RAN (examples):
- sudo journalctl -k -S "2026-08-21 14:00" | grep -i vxlan
- sudo cat /sys/class/net/vxlan0/statistics/rx_errors
- sudo ethtool -S eth0 | grep vxlan
- curl -sS -X POST "https://console.internal/rollouts/325/pause" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}"

POST-INCIDENT NOTES (lessons learned):
- Overlay offload behaviour is hardware-sensitive. We must test policy rollouts with a matrix of NIC models (QX-9xx is now on the matrix).
- Small changes to L4 matching can cause large overlay churn if the rollout is too aggressive. Canary pacing matters.
- Agent reconnect storms amplify the problem — add jitter and backoff improvements to agent boot/reconnect logic.

UNKNOWN / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Are there other NIC models with similar offload edge-cases? (Lin to run inventory by 2026-08-27)
- Can we detect offload table saturation proactively from sFlow counters before kernel messages? (Investigate)

COMMUNICATIONS LOG:
- 14:11: Briefed customer A's technical contact (email + call). They accepted rollback and temporary pinning.
- 15:00: Post-mortem scheduled with customer for 2026-08-26.

ATTACHMENTS / REFERENCES:
- sFlow dump (zone-3 14:00-14:20) -> see linked artifact JIRA-5827 attachment
- vendor bug DB (QX-9xx vxlan offload overflow) referenced in confluence link above

NEXT STEPS (short):
- Draft VXLAN offload runbook and push to confluence (Priya).
- Add rollout simulator ticket (Miguel).
- Coordinate vendor test window (Lin).
- Update canary default from 20% to 10% for tenant policy rollouts until we have vendor patch.

NOTES TO SELF / ONCALL SCRATCHES:
- When triaging similar incidents, start with netdev counters + agent reconnects before assuming BGP/MTU.
- Keep a small repo of safe netplan fragments for temporary pinning (store under infra/playbooks/vxlan-pinning).

END OF JOURNAL.
